safety_wire_by_hand:task.criterion:
Assess the completed hand-installed safety wire on the bolts as one finished assembly. Do not grade point by point.

Return:
Result: PASS, FAIL, or INSUFFICIENT IMAGE
Score: 0–100
Reasoning: 2–4 sentences describing the strongest visible evidence.

Consider the installation as a whole:
• Functional routing and tightening direction: 40%
• Seating, tautness, and security around bolt heads: 25%
• Twist consistency and general workmanship: 20%
• Safe pigtail termination: 15%

PASS requires 75 or higher and no critical defect.

Critical defects:
• Wire clearly tends to loosen a bolt.
• Wire clearly misses a required bolt hole.
• Obvious slack or a loop rising over a bolt head.
• Broken or severely damaged wire.
• Exposed sharp termination.

Expected workmanship includes tight, even twists, approximately 6–8 twists per inch, and a bent-back pigtail. Without a ruler, estimate twist density; do not fail solely because an exact count cannot be measured. Minor cosmetic unevenness should reduce the score, not automatically fail.

Use INSUFFICIENT IMAGE only when the overall installation cannot reasonably be judged.

safety_wire_pliers_1:task.criterion:
Assess the completed safety-wire installation on the bolts as one finished assembly. Do not grade individual steps or attempt to prove that safety-wire pliers were used.

Return:
Result: PASS, FAIL, or INSUFFICIENT IMAGE
Score: 0–100
Reasoning: 2–4 sentences describing the strongest visible evidence.

Score the overall result:
• Functional routing and tightening direction: 40%
• Seating, tautness, and security: 25%
• Twist consistency and workmanship: 20%
• Safe pigtail termination: 15%

PASS requires 75 or higher and no critical defect.

Critical defects:
• Wire clearly pulls either bolt toward loosening.
• Wire does not visibly engage both required bolt holes.
• Obvious slack or wire capable of lifting over a bolt head.
• Broken, severely kinked, or damaged wire.
• Sharp exposed pigtail.

The main run should appear tight and evenly twisted, approximately 6–8 twists per inch. The pigtail should be compact, defined, and bent back or under. Estimate dimensions when no scale is present. Do not automatically fail minor unevenness, uncertain exact twist count, or absence of visible evidence of the gator-roll technique.

Use INSUFFICIENT IMAGE only when the overall result cannot be judged.

insert_wire_for_double_wrap_turnbuckle_s.criterion:
Grade one final photo of a turnbuckle safetied by the double-wrap wire method.

Return:
Result: PASS or FAIL
Reasoning: 2–4 sentences.
Failed/unverifiable criteria: list.

PASS only if clearly visible:

1. Entire turnbuckle, both terminals, barrel hole, terminal safety holes, all wire runs, all four terminations, exposed threads, and ruler are sharp and unobstructed.
2. Two separate wires pass through the barrel and extend toward opposite ends on opposite sides.
3. Wires route in opposite directions through the terminal eyes, forks, or swaged-terminal holes.
4. Runs lie closely along the barrel and form a streamlined, approximately symmetrical installation.
5. Wire appears tight without slack, severe kinks, damage, or unnecessary loops.
6. Every terminal wrapping has at least four tight, uniform turns.
7. Wraps are closely formed without visible gaps.
8. Cut ends are bent inward and create no snag or sharp hazard.
9. No more than three terminal threads are exposed at either end.

FAIL any unmet criterion. Use “FAIL — insufficient visual evidence” when required areas are hidden or unclear. Do not infer cable tension, wire diameter, adjustment, or wire newness.

wire_safety_on_bolts_by_hand — VLM GRADING CRITERIA
Assess the completed hand-twisted safety wire installation joining two bolt heads, with pigtail visible in the image. Evaluate each criterion independently as PASS or FAIL.

Criteria
1. The wire between the bolt heads is untwisted, running as two straight un-braided strands between bolt holes.
2. Twists between bolts are uneven, showing 1–3 wraps per inch measured against a rule in frame.
3. The wire loop rides up over the top rim of the bolt head.
4. Pigtail at the end stands straight out away from the bolt head.
5. The finished work shows this defect: Wire between bolts hangs slack or visibly loose.
6. The finished work shows this defect: Pigtail end sticks straight out unbent as a snag.
7. The finished work shows this defect: Wire is kinked, frayed, or broken along its run.

Overall decision
Overall PASS requires every required criterion to pass and no critical defect. Mark an unobservable required criterion “FAIL — not demonstrated in image.” Evaluate only visible evidence and do not infer hidden measurements, internal damage, torque, pressure, or test results.

wire_safety_on_bolts_with_safety_wire_pliers — VLM GRADING CRITERIA
Assess the completed safety wire installation joining two bolt heads, twisted with safety wire pliers and finished with a pigtail visible in the image. Evaluate each criterion independently as PASS or FAIL.

Criteria
1. A single continuous untwisted wire pair links two bolt holes.
2. Twists between the bolts are uneven and discontinuous, leaving a loose untwisted slack span.
3. Twist density measured against a rule or scale in frame shows 1-3 wraps per inch.
4. Pigtail end stands straight out away from the bolt head, not bent back.
5. The finished work shows this defect: The wire loop rides up over the bolt head, leaving a slack loop.
6. The finished work shows this defect: A wire strand is visibly broken, kinked, or frayed.
7. The finished work shows this defect: The cut pigtail end stands straight out unbent as a snag hazard.

Overall decision
Overall PASS requires every required criterion to pass and no critical defect. Mark an unobservable required criterion “FAIL — not demonstrated in image.” Evaluate only visible evidence and do not infer hidden measurements, internal damage, torque, pressure, or test results.

negative.criterion:
wire_safety_on_a_turnbuckle_by_hand — VLM GRADING CRITERIA
Assess the completed double-wrap safety wire installed by hand on a turnbuckle barrel and both end terminals visible in the image. Evaluate each criterion independently as PASS or FAIL.

Criteria
1. Two separate safety wires pass through the turnbuckle barrel hole, lying together on the same side.
2. Wire strands bow away from the barrel, forming slack loops standing off from the surface.
3. Each wrapped end shows fewer than four coils around the shank, separated by visible gaps.
4. Cut wire ends project straight outward from the shank, standing out.
5. The finished work shows this defect: Wire ends are bare, straight and sharp, projecting away from the shank.
6. The finished work shows this defect: A safety wire is broken, or missing from one end of the turnbuckle.
7. The finished work shows this defect: Wraps are loose or spread with visible gaps, leaving the wire slack.

Overall decision
Overall PASS requires every required criterion to pass and no critical defect. Mark an unobservable required criterion “FAIL — not demonstrated in image.” Evaluate only visible evidence and do not infer hidden measurements, internal damage, torque, pressure, or test results.
